title: Selective Off-Policy Reference Tuning with Plan Guidance
claim: Our method improves reward while avoiding the response-length growth and entropy instability that competing guided-training baselines exhibit.
layout: 3x3 grid of line plots; columns are backbones, rows are metrics; shared legend
description: A 3-by-3 grid of line charts showing training dynamics over 500 optimization steps. Columns are three backbones: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct. Rows are training reward, response length and entropy, with step on the x-axis at the bottom. Each panel has five noisy curves: GRPO (blue), LUFFY (orange), ReLIFT (purple), Scaf-GRPO (green) and SORT (red). The legend sits inside the top-right panel. SORT, in red, rises steadily in reward. Its response length stays low and flat, while LUFFY and ReLIFT grow to much longer responses. Entropy curves differ widely: some spike or collapse and SORT stays moderate. The eye goes first to the red SORT lines and the orange and purple curves that diverge upward in the length row.
caption: Training dynamics across 500 optimization steps. Rows show reward, response length, and entropy; columns show the three backbones. SORT improves reward without the length expansion seen in LUFFY and ReLIFT.
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards helps reasoning, but GRPO-style methods stall on hard prompts where all sampled rollouts fail. SORT adds a repair update for those failures without changing rollout generation: it derives a plan from the reference solution, compares token probabilities with and without that plan, and gives higher weight to tokens that become more predictable under plan conditioning. This turns all-wrong prompts into selective, structure-aware learning signals instead of uniform imitation. Across three backbones and eight reasoning benchmarks, SORT improves over GRPO and guidance baselines, with largest gains on weaker models.
